name: Joan d’Arc

text: Joan d'Arc was a French heroine. She was born about 1412 in the rural north of Lorraine, where old beliefs survived as superstition beside Christianity. Early in life she began to hear voices, two female and one male, which she took for saints. About age fifteen she dressed as a man and rode to the Dauphin, the embattled heir to the French throne. The Dauphin made her his general. At the head of her soldiers she fought the English at Orleans and lifted the siege of the city. For this she earned the title Maid of Orleans. A year later the Dauphin was crowned Charles VII with Joan at his side. She was captured and sold to the English, then tried for witchcraft because she refused to deny her voices. She was burned at the stake in 1431, before she turned twenty. Twenty-five years later the church held a posthumous trial and declared her innocent. She was canonized in 1920. Her inquisitors asked what she knew of the fairy faith. She insisted her voices were saints, not fairies.
objective: Document Joan d'Arc as a French heroine whose story carries Celtic motifs.
